result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A makes the key idea easiest to find: the intro says to mix around the peak, and the diagram marks a mixing window from just before the peak up to it. Its timing is given only as a rough 4 to 8 hour range that it says may differ. B has a more detailed diagram with axes and good stage cards, but it uses an exact 12-hour scale and per-stage hour ranges, with only a short caption saying your hours will differ. Both diagrams have small spots where labels touch the curve: A's 'Still usable' note and B's '1 · Fed' and 'tide line' labels. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both pages have a clean diagram with the stages labelled directly in shaded bands and a highlighted mixing window. B puts the key idea up front, in bold in the intro and again under 'Why timing matters'. It also avoids precise hours, saying only 'around 4 to 8 hours… yours may differ.' A has a numbered 0–12 hour axis, a title that promises 'Hour by Hour', and an odd uptick at the end of the curve, although it does say 'your hours will differ'. In both, some text overlaps the curve: A's 'tide line' note and B's 'Still usable' note.
